questions.title: Why does GRPO's token‑level importance weight violate the principle of importance sampling?
questions.question_body: The paper argues that GRPO applies the importance weight \( w_{i,t}(\theta)=\frac{\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\theta_{old}}(y_{i,t}\mid x,y_{i,<t})} \) at each token, but importance sampling requires averaging over many samples from the behavior distribution. Could someone explain in detail why using a single‑sample weight per token is mathematically incorrect and how this leads to high‑variance gradients?

questions.title: How is the sequence‑level importance ratio \( s_i(\theta) \) derived and why is length normalization needed?
questions.question_body: GSPO defines \( s_i(\theta)=\left( \frac{\pi_{\theta}(y_i|x)}{\pi_{\theta_{old}}(y_i|x)} \right)^{1/|y_i|}=\exp\left( \frac{1}{|y_i|}\sum_{t}\log \frac{\pi_{\theta}(y_{i,t}|x,y_{i,<t})}{\pi_{\theta_{old}}(y_{i,t}|x,y_{i,<t})}\right) \). I understand the exponentiation is a length‑normalization, but I'm unclear on two points: (1) why taking the \(1/|y_i|\) power yields a more stable importance ratio, and (2) what would happen if we omitted this normalization – e.g., how would the clipping range need to change?

questions.title: What exactly is the "group‑based advantage" used in GSPO and how does it differ from token‑wise advantages in PPO?
questions.question_body: The paper computes \( \widehat{A}_i = \frac{r(x,y_i)-\text{mean}\{r(x,y_j)\}}{\text{std}\{r(x,y_j)\}} \) across a group of responses. In PPO we normally have a value model that gives a token‑level advantage \( \widehat{A}_t \). Why is it valid to share the same advantage for all tokens of a response, and does this affect bias or variance of the gradient estimator?

questions.title: Can anyone clarify the gradient derivation for GSPO (Eq. 13) and why the importance ratio appears outside the log‑gradient term?
questions.question_body:
In Eq. 13 the gradient is written as
\[ \nabla_\theta J_{GSPO}= \mathbb{E}[ s_i(\theta)\widehat{A}_i \nabla_\theta \log s_i(\theta)] .\]
Given that \( s_i(\theta) = (\pi_θ(y_i|x)/
π_{old}(y_i|x))^{1/|y_i|} \), how do we expand \( \nabla_θ \log s_i(θ) \) to obtain the sum over token log‑gradients shown in Eq. 14? A step‑by‑step derivation would help.

questions.title: Why does GSPO clip a much larger fraction of tokens yet achieve higher training efficiency than GRPO?
questions.question_body: Figure 3 in the paper shows that GSPO discards two orders of magnitude more tokens due to clipping, but still learns faster. Is this because the remaining (unclipped) tokens have lower variance gradients, or does sequence‑level clipping provide a better signal? How can we quantitatively relate the fraction of clipped samples to gradient variance in both algorithms?

questions.title: How does expert‑activation volatility in MoE models break GRPO’s token‑level importance weights?
questions.question_body: The authors state that after each update about 10 % of experts activated for a token change, causing large fluctuations in \( w_{i,t}(θ) \). Could someone explain mechanistically why a change in routing leads to an unstable importance ratio, and why GSPO’s sequence‑level ratio is immune to this effect?

questions.title: What is the ‘Routing Replay’ strategy and why is it unnecessary for GSPO?
questions.question_body: In GRPO training of MoE models, Routing Replay caches old routing decisions and reuses them when computing \( w_{i,t}(θ) \). How exactly is this implemented (e.g., which tensors are stored, how are they combined with the new policy), and why does GSPO not need such replay buffers? Is it simply because GSPO never looks at token‑level likelihoods?

questions.title: How can inference‑engine likelihoods be used directly in GSPO without recomputation?
questions.question_body: The paper claims that sequence‑level likelihoods are tolerant to precision differences between training and inference engines, allowing us to skip recomputing \( π_{old}(y|x) \). What are the practical steps to retrieve these likelihoods from an inference engine like vLLM, and what precision issues might still affect the importance ratio?

questions.title: When would one prefer GSPO-token over plain GSPO?
questions.question_body: GSPO-token introduces per‑token advantages while keeping the same sequence‑level importance ratio. In what scenarios (e.g., multi‑turn dialogue, fine‑grained reward shaping) does this flexibility provide a measurable benefit, and does it reintroduce any of GRPO’s instability?

questions.title: Is there a theoretical connection between GSPO and standard REINFORCE with baseline subtraction?
questions.question_body: GSPO’s objective resembles a weighted REINFORCE estimator where the weight is the clipped sequence importance ratio. Can we view GSPO as REINFORCE with an adaptive baseline equal to the group mean reward? If so, does this interpretation suggest any alternative variance‑reduction techniques?
